mainTopic: Mixtures of blood from different קרבנות: whether the עולה's place serves for שירים, and a new משנה on mixing inner and outer blood
overview: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that explains why the תורה says 'דם' twice. The repetition teaches that עולה blood mixed with blood of any other קרבן is still placed on the מזבח, even the blood of a בכור, מעשר or פסח. The גמרא tries to prove from this that the place for עולה blood also works for leftover blood (שירים), but it pushes the proof aside. It then explains that תנאים disagree about which פסוק teaches that the blood of קרבנות does not cancel each other out. Next, the גמרא tries a second proof from a ברייתא about mixed blood placed above the red line. Scholars from ארץ ישראל read that ברייתא differently, and the גמרא debates whether it can be used here at all. A new משנה then rules that blood meant for inside the היכל that got mixed with blood meant for outside is poured out, and records a מחלוקת about the case where it was placed inside first. The גמרא explains that רבי אליעזר does not argue here, because inside blood must come before outside blood.

steps.title: Why does the verse say 'blood' twice?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why 'דם' is repeated. It explains that one mention alone might only cover עולה blood mixed with its own תמורה. So how would we include תודה and שלמים?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the verse say 'blood,' 'blood'? With only one mention, I might have said it only covers an עולה mixed with its substitute, since even while alive they can be offered together. From where do we include a תודה or שלמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא opens with a question about the double word 'דם' and starts building a step-by-step list of cases. This is a setup: it shows which case is easiest, before moving to harder ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה and its תמורה are really the same kind of קרבן, so mixing their blood is no problem at all. Even live animals of these two kinds can simply be offered together. A תודה or שלמים is a different kind of קרבן, so the ברייתא asks where we learn that their blood, mixed with an עולה's blood, may also be placed on the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches / the verse says
A substitute animal declared in place of a קרבן; it takes the same status
Got mixed together
While still alive
To include (an extra case)

phrases.english: Why does the verse say "blood," "blood"?
For one might have thought: I only have
these, where it got mixed with its substitute,
phrases.notes: Here 'it' is the עולה, and its substitute is its תמורה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the quoted ברייתא, which the גמרא brings as a possible proof for its question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What source includes עולה blood mixed with blood of תודה or שלמים, which are a different kind of קרבן than the עולה?

steps.title: Including תודה and שלמים, then asking about אשם
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says it could include תודה and שלמים from the first 'דם', since like an עולה they come as a נדר or נדבה. Then it asks where we include an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: I can include a תודה and שלמים, since they come as a vow or a gift offering just like an עולה. But from where do we include the אשם?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא climbs one step up its ladder. It finds a reason to include תודה and שלמים, then raises a harder case: the אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תודה and שלמים are similar to an עולה because a person can bring any of them voluntarily, as a נדר or נדבה. An אשם is never voluntary. It comes only to atone, so that shared feature is missing. That makes the אשם a harder case to include.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow: 'I take upon myself to bring a קרבן'
A gift offering: 'this animal is a קרבן'
Like it (like the עולה)
Guilt offering

phrases.english: I can include a thanks offering and peace offerings,
since they come as a vow or a gift offering, like it.
From where do we include the guilt offering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 1's question with a similarity, then pushes to a harder case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What source includes עולה blood mixed with אשם blood, given that an אשם is never voluntary?

steps.title: אשם is included too; the second 'blood' covers בכור, מעשר and פסח
steps.stepSummary: The אשם could come from the first 'דם', since its blood also gets מתן ארבע like an עולה. But בכור, מעשר and פסח have only one placing of blood, so the second 'דם' is needed for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: I can include the אשם, since it needs four placings of blood like an עולה. But from where do we include a בכור, מעשר and פסח? The verse says 'blood,' 'blood.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its ladder. It explains that the hardest cases, בכור, מעשר and פסח, are the reason the תורה wrote 'דם' a second time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אשם matches the עולה in how its blood is placed: two placings that cover all four sides of the מזבח (מתן ארבע). בכור, מעשר and פסח get only a single placing, so they share nothing with the עולה. Only the extra word 'דם' can include them. The result: עולה blood mixed with any of these is placed on the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: Placing blood so it reaches all four sides of the מזבח (done as two corner placings)
Requires
Firstborn animal offering
Animal tithe offering
The Pesach offering

steps.whatToRemember: The first 'דם' covers קרבנות similar to the עולה: its תמורה, תודה and שלמים, and the אשם. The second 'דם' is needed for בכור, מעשר and פסח, whose blood gets only one placing.

phrases.english: I can include the guilt offering,
since it requires four placings, like it.
phrases.notes: 'Four' means two corner placings that reach all four sides of the מזבח, the same as an עולה.

phrases.english: From where do we include the firstborn, tithe and Pesach offering?
The verse says "blood," "blood."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the אשם question and then gives the final answer to the ברייתא's opening question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second 'דם' teaches that עולה blood mixed even with blood of בכור, מעשר or פסח (one placing only) is still placed on the מזבח.

steps.title: Proof that the עולה's place also works for leftover blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא includes even a mix of the final part of an עולה's blood with a בכור's blood. If so, the place for עולה blood must also be a proper place for leftover blood (שירים).
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't the ברייתא talking even about the end of an עולה's blood mixed with a בכור? If so, we learn that the place of the עולה is also the place of the leftovers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now uses the ברייתא as a proof for its earlier question: can the spot where עולה blood is placed also serve as the spot for leftover blood?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a mixture of עולה blood and בכור blood is placed on the מזבח, in the way the עולה's blood is placed. The גמרא suggests this covers even a case where the בכור's blood in the mix counts only as leftover blood (שירים). The ברייתא still allows placing the mixture. That would show the עולה's place counts as a proper place for שירים.

keyTerms.meaning: What, is it not…? (the גמרא suggests a reading)
The end / the final part
And learn from it
Leftover blood remaining after the required placings

steps.confusionAlert: 'מאי לאו' only suggests a reading of the ברייתא. It is a proof attempt, and the next step pushes it aside.

phrases.english: What, is it not talking about the end of an עולה with a בכור,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: מְקוֹם עוֹלָה מְקוֹם שִׁירַיִם?
phrases.english: and learn from it: the place of the עולה is the place of leftovers?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the ברייתא's conclusion about בכור into a proof for the גמרא's question about שירים.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the place for placing עולה blood also counts as a proper place for leftover blood (שירים).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's ruling, from the double 'דם', that עולה blood mixed with בכור blood is placed on the מזבח.

steps.title: No, the ברייתא means the first blood of an עולה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from Step 4. The ברייתא may be talking about the first blood of an עולה mixed with a בכור's blood, not the leftover blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The ברייתא is talking about the first blood of an עולה mixed with the blood of a בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the proof from Step 4 does not work. The ברייתא could be talking about a different mixture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 assumed the ברייתא covered the last part of the עולה's blood, which would tell us something about where שירים go. Now the גמרא says it may be the first, main blood of the עולה. If so, the ברייתא says nothing about שירים at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The first blood that comes out of an עולה, the main blood used for the placings
A firstborn animal brought as an offering; its blood is placed only once

phrases.english: No; it means the first blood of a burnt offering mixed with a firstborn's blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from Step 4 by reading the case differently
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that the place for עולה blood is also a proper place for שירים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be read as talking about the first blood of the עולה, not the last part

steps.title: Then what new thing is the ברייתא teaching?
steps.stepSummary: If the case is the first blood of an עולה with a בכור, the only lesson is that the two bloods do not cancel each other out. But we already learn that from the יום כיפור פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what is it teaching us? That the bloods of offerings that go on the מזבח do not cancel each other out? We already learn that from 'And he shall take of the blood of the bull and of the blood of the goat'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading from Step 5. If that is the case, the ברייתא seems to teach nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום כיפור the כהן גדול mixes the bull's blood with the goat's blood, and both still count. That already shows that two kinds of offering blood do not cancel each other out. So why would the ברייתא need the extra word 'דם' to teach it?

keyTerms.meaning: What is it teaching us? This asks what the new point is.

keyTerms.term: אֵין עוֹלִין מְבַטְּלִין זֶה אֶת זֶה
keyTerms.meaning: Things that go on the מזבח do not cancel each other out
It comes out from, it is learned from

phrases.english: And what is it teaching us?

phrases.aramaic: אֵין עוֹלִין מְבַטְּלִין זֶה אֶת זֶה?
phrases.english: That things that go on the altar do not cancel each other out?

phrases.aramaic: מִ״וְּלָקַח מִדַּם הַפָּר וּמִדַּם הַשָּׂעִיר״ נָפְקָא!
phrases.english: We learn that from 'And he shall take of the blood of the bull and of the blood of the goat'!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:18. This is the יום כיפור service, where the two bloods get mixed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading given in Step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the ברייתא is about the first blood of an עולה mixed with a בכור's blood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On that reading the ברייתא teaches only אין עולין מבטלין, which is already known from ויקרא 16:18, so the extra word 'דם' would be unneeded

steps.title: תנאים disagree about the source
steps.stepSummary: Different תנאים learn the same rule from different פסוקים. The ברייתא follows the one who learns it from 'דם' 'דם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a disagreement between תנאים. One learns it from here, and another learns it from there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 6. Everyone agrees on the rule, but תנאים disagree about which פסוק teaches it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not repeating something already known. It follows a תנא who does not use the יום כיפור פסוק for this rule. For that תנא, the repeated 'דם' is the real source.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a disagreement between תנאים
There is one who learns it from here

phrases.english: It is a disagreement between tanna'im;
there is one who learns it from here,
and there is one who learns it from there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in Step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Disagreement among תנאים about the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule is learned only from ויקרא 16:18, so the ברייתא would be repeating it
steps.terutzMaskana: Different תנאים learn the rule from different פסוקים, and the ברייתא follows the one who uses 'דם' 'דם'
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees on the rule אין עולין מבטלין זה את זה. The argument is only about which פסוק teaches it.

steps.title: Why these תנאים skip the other two פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: The תנאים who use 'קדש הם' do not learn from the יום כיפור פסוק, because they hold the bloods are not mixed for the corners. They also do not learn anything from 'דם' 'דם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: These other תנאים do not learn from 'And he shall take of the blood of the bull and of the blood of the goat,' because they hold that the bloods are not mixed for the corners. They do not learn from 'blood,' 'blood,' because they do not read any lesson into that repetition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains why the other group of תנאים does not use the two פסוקים we just saw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יום כיפור פסוק only proves the rule if the two bloods are mixed. These תנאים hold that each blood is placed on the corners of the golden מזבח separately, so there is no mixture and no proof. They also do not draw any lesson from the repeated word 'דם'.

keyTerms.meaning: They learn, they derive
The bloods are not mixed for placing on the corners of the מזבח
It does not mean anything to them; they read no lesson into it

phrases.english: And these tanna'im,
phrases.notes: He means the תנאים who learn the rule from 'קדש הם' (במדבר 18:17).

phrases.aramaic: מִ״וְּלָקַח מִדַּם הַפָּר וּמִדַּם הַשָּׂעִיר״ לָא יָלְפִי –
phrases.english: do not learn it from 'And he shall take of the blood of the bull and of the blood of the goat'
because they hold that the bloods are not mixed for the corners;
he does not learn it from 'blood,' 'blood'
because they do not learn anything from 'blood,' 'blood.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 7 by explaining how each group of תנאים avoids the other פסוקים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנאים who use 'קדש הם' reject ויקרא 16:18 because they hold אין מערבין לקרנות, and they reject 'דם' 'דם' because they read no lesson into the repetition

steps.title: Why don't the others learn it from 'קדש הם'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks the opposite question. Why do the other תנאים not learn the rule from 'קדש הם'?
steps.simpleTranslation: But from 'they are holy,' what is the reason they do not learn it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other side. It asks why the תנאים who use the other two פסוקים do not also use 'קדש הם'. The next step gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we see why one group skips the other פסוקים, we need to know why the other groups skip 'קדש הם'. Each side must have a reason the other side's פסוק does not work for them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They are holy' (במדבר 18:17), said about בכור animals
What is the reason?

phrases.english: But from 'they are holy'
what is the reason they do not learn it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִ״קֹּדֶשׁ הֵם״ מַאי טַעְמָא לָא יָלְפִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the same question as Step 8, but about the other group of תנאים
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the תנאים who use 'דם' 'דם' or ויקרא 16:18 do not use 'קדש הם'

steps.title: 'קדש הם' teaches about substitutes
steps.stepSummary: They use 'קדש הם' for a different lesson. The בכור itself is offered, but its substitute is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They hold that 'they are holy' means: they themselves are offered, but their substitutes are not offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 9. These תנאים need 'קדש הם' for a different law, so it is not free to teach our rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'הם' (they) teaches that only the בכור animals themselves are brought on the מזבח. An animal swapped for them, a תמורה, is not brought. Since the פסוק is used up on this lesson, it cannot also teach אין עולין מבטלין.

keyTerms.meaning: Because they hold
An animal someone tried to swap for a holy animal; it becomes holy too
Are offered on the מזבח

phrases.english: They hold that 'they are holy' means:
they are offered, but their substitutes are not offered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה in Step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They use 'קדש הם' to teach that a בכור's תמורה is not offered, so the פסוק is not available for אין עולין מבטלין

steps.title: The other תנא learns the substitute law from a different פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The תנא who uses 'קדש הם' for our rule learns the substitute law from 'אם שור אם שה לה׳ הוא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one learns it from 'Whether it be ox or sheep, it is the Lord's': it is offered, but its substitute is not offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the תנא who uses 'קדש הם' for אין עולין מבטלין still knows that a בכור's substitute is not offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a question hidden here: where does this תנא learn the substitute law? He learns it from the word 'הוא' (it) in a different פסוק about the בכור. That leaves 'קדש הם' free to teach that the bloods do not cancel each other out.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one, the other opinion

keyTerms.term: אִם שׁוֹר אִם שֶׂה לַה׳ הוּא
keyTerms.meaning: 'Whether it be ox or sheep, it is the Lord's' (ויקרא 27:26)

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree that a בכור's תמורה is not offered. They only disagree about which פסוק teaches it, and that decides whether 'קדש הם' is free to teach אין עולין מבטלין.

phrases.english: And the other one,
phrases.notes: The question is skipped here: how does the תנא who uses 'קדש הם' for our rule learn the law about the substitute?

phrases.aramaic: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מֵ״אִם שׁוֹר אִם שֶׂה לַה׳ הוּא״ –
phrases.english: learns it from 'Whether it be ox or sheep, it is the Lord's':
it is offered, but its substitute is not offered.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ, נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מֵ״אִם שׁוֹר אִם שֶׂה לַה׳ הוּא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the hidden question raised by Step 10 about the תנא who uses 'קדש הם' for אין עולין מבטלין
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He learns that a תמורה is not offered from 'הוא' in ויקרא 27:26, which leaves 'קדש הם' free for אין עולין מבטלין

steps.title: Quoting a ברייתא about mixed blood put above the line
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: if a כהן put mixed blood above the red line without asking, everyone agrees he now puts blood below the line, and both count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If the כהן put the blood above and did not ask first, these and those agree that he should go back and put blood below. Both of these count for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to use as a proof. This step only sets up the source. The proof itself comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is blood that goes above the red line mixed with blood that goes below it. The כהן already put some above without asking the חכמים. Both sides of the earlier מחלוקת agree he now puts the rest below, and both placements count.

keyTerms.meaning: Above or below the red line around the מזבח
Asked the חכמים before acting
They count for him and work as proper placements

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If he put the blood above and did not ask first,
phrases.notes: This is mixed blood. Part of it belongs above the red line and part belongs below it.

phrases.english: these and those agree
phrases.notes: Both sides of the argument: the חכמים and רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: that he should go back and put blood below,
and both of these count for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the open question about the place of עולה blood versus the place of שירים.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the place of עולה blood is the same as the place of שירים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about mixed blood put above the line without asking

steps.title: Drawing the proof from the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the ברייתא as a mix of חטאת and עולה blood. It concludes that the עולה's spot is the same as the שירים spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this about a חטאת and a עולה that got mixed? Once he put blood above, what is left counts as שירים of the חטאת. Yet the ברייתא says he puts blood below. Learn from this that the place of a עולה is the place of שירים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the ברייתא proves that עולה blood and שירים go in the same place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once some of the mixture was put above for the חטאת, the rest of the חטאת's blood is now only שירים. So the mixture left over is עולה blood plus שירים. The ברייתא says to put it below, so one placement must work for both. That means their places are the same.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it so that...: introduces the reading the proof depends on
The blood left over after the main placements, poured at the base of the מזבח
And learn from it: this is the conclusion of the proof

phrases.english: What, is it not where a חטאת and a עולה were mixed?
And once he put it above,
the rest of the חטאת's blood becomes שירים;
and it teaches: these and those agree
that he goes back and puts blood below,
so learn from it:
the place of the עולה is the place of the שירים!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the proof out of the ברייתא quoted in step 12.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling that the leftover mixture is put below the line

steps.title: In ארץ ישראל they explain the ברייתא differently
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר יוסף reports that in ארץ ישראל they say the ברייתא is about an outer חטאת mixed with שירים, not with a עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב יצחק בר יוסף came, he said: In the West they say, what case are we dealing with here? A case where an outer חטאת got mixed with שירים.
steps.whatsHappening: The proof is pushed aside by changing what the ברייתא is about. There is no עולה blood in the mixture at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the mixture is outer חטאת blood plus שירים, then once blood is put above, everything left is שירים. שירים obviously go below. So the ברייתא tells us nothing about where עולה blood goes.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning the scholars of ארץ ישראל
What case are we dealing with here? This narrows the case to answer a question
A חטאת whose blood is put on the outer מזבח, above the line

steps.whatToRemember: The proof falls away because the ברייתא may be about a mixture of חטאת blood and שירים, with no עולה involved.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף, אֲמַר:
phrases.english: When רב יצחק בר יוסף came, he said:
They say in the West,
what case are we dealing with here?
A case where an outer חטאת got mixed with שירים.
phrases.notes: Here שירים means the leftover blood of a חטאת whose blood is brought inside. That leftover blood is poured at the outer מזבח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 13 by reading the ברייתא as a different case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא only
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed the mixture had עולה blood, but it could be חטאת blood with שירים.

steps.title: אביי asks why not use plain outer שירים
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks why the case is not simply a חטאת mixed with the שירים of an outer חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Let the Master say a case where it got mixed with שירים!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי questions the case that was chosen. He suggests a simpler one that would answer the question just as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leftover blood from an outer חטאת would also leave only שירים after the placement above. So why bring in the שירים of an inner חטאת at all? אביי is asking what this choice adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the Master say: suggests a simpler explanation

phrases.english: אביי said to him,
let the Master say: a case where it got mixed with שירים!
phrases.notes: אביי means the שירים of an ordinary outer חטאת, not one whose blood is brought inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the specific case chosen in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using the שירים of an inner חטאת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A simpler case with outer שירים would solve the problem just as well.

steps.title: The case teaches that missing שירים do not hold things back
steps.stepSummary: אביי himself suggests that the case teaches something new. Even someone who holds that inner שירים hold back the קרבן agrees that a shortage of them does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps this is what it teaches us: even according to the one who says שירים hold it back, if they are lacking, they do not hold it back.
steps.whatsHappening: This explains why the case uses the שירים of an inner חטאת. It shows that a shortage of שירים does not ruin the קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some blood of the mixture was put above, so less of the inner שירים reaches the base. The ברייתא still lets it count. That shows a shortage of שירים is fine, even according to the view that skipping them entirely holds the קרבן back.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps
This is what it teaches us
Hold back, so the קרבן is not valid without them
They were lacking, meaning some of them are missing

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up two different things: skipping the שירים entirely, which is the argument about מעכבין, and having less שירים than usual. Only the second is said here not to hold the קרבן back.

phrases.english: Perhaps this is what it teaches us:
even according to the one who says שירים hold it back,
if they are lacking, they do not hold it back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: אביי himself suggests an answer to his own question from step 15 by showing what the chosen case adds.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the chosen case teaches a new הלכה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Picking inner שירים seemed pointless, since outer שירים would work just as well.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case teaches that a shortage of inner שירים does not hold back the קרבן, even for the one who says שירים are מעכבין.

steps.title: רבא תוספאה: that ברייתא was already explained differently
steps.stepSummary: רבא תוספאה objects to רבינא that the ברייתא cannot prove anything here. It was already explained as a case where most of the blood was 'upper' blood and the כהן put enough above to cover the 'lower' blood and a bit more.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא תוספאה said to רבינא: We already explained that ברייתא as a case where most of the blood is upper blood, and the כהן put above the red line the amount of the lower blood plus a little more!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא תוספאה challenges the proof that was drawn from the ברייתא in the earlier steps. He says the ברייתא was already set up in a special way that has nothing to do with our question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא is about a mixture that is mostly upper blood, and enough was put above to be sure some upper blood went up, it is a narrow special case. Then it cannot be used for the question of the עולה's place and the שירים at all. רבא תוספאה is asking how the ברייתא could be brought into this discussion in the first place.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, here questioning רבינא
We set it up / we explained it as a specific case
Blood that goes above the red line
Blood that goes below the red line
A measured amount

phrases.english: Rava Tosfa'a said to Ravina:
But we already explained that one
phrases.notes: "That one" is the ברייתא from the earlier steps, about the כהן who put mixed blood above the line without asking.

phrases.english: as a case with a majority of upper blood,
and he puts above
the amount of the lower blood and a bit more!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא used as the proof in steps 12–13.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using the ברייתא as proof about where the עולה and the שירים go
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא was already set up as a narrow case (mostly upper blood, plus an amount put above), so it cannot serve as a general proof.

steps.title: רבינא: that explanation followed a rejected approach
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that the old explanation of the ברייתא was only needed by those who first thought the argument was about mixed blood. Once the conclusion was that the argument is about cups, that explanation was dropped.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: That explanation applies to those who said at first that there is no mixing. But by the conclusion, they argue about cups.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא defends bringing the ברייתא into this discussion. The narrow explanation of the ברייתא belonged to an approach that the גמרא later dropped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first, the argument between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים was understood as being about blood poured together, with רבי אליעזר holding אין בילה. In the end it was understood as being about separate cups that got switched. Under that conclusion, the ברייתא no longer needs the 'mostly upper blood' setup, so it was fair to bring it into the discussion of the עולה's place and the שירים.

keyTerms.meaning: This statement applies only…
At first, in the earlier approach
There is no mixing; the blood does not count as evenly mixed
The final conclusion
Cups of blood

steps.whatToRemember: An explanation that was made to fit an approach the גמרא later rejected falls away together with that approach.

phrases.english: He said to him:
That applies according to those who said
at first that there is no mixing;
phrases.notes: This was the earlier way of reading רבי אליעזר's view: blood poured together does not count as evenly mixed.

phrases.english: by the conclusion, they argue about cups.
phrases.notes: He means separate cups of blood that got switched, not blood poured together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא תוספאה's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The earlier explanation depended on an approach that was rejected
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא must be read as mostly upper blood, so it proves nothing
steps.terutzMaskana: By the conclusion (the argument is about cups), that narrow reading is not needed, so the ברייתא may properly be brought into this discussion (though its proof was already turned aside in step 14)

steps.title: משנה: inner blood mixed with outer blood
steps.stepSummary: Blood meant for inside the היכל that got mixed with blood meant for the outer altar must be poured into the drain. If the כהן put it outside first and then inside, the offering is fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Blood meant to be put inside that got mixed with blood meant to be put outside should be poured into the drain. If he put it outside and then put it inside, it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules on a mixture of blood from inner offerings and blood from outer offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since each blood must go only to its own place, the mixture cannot be used ahead of time, so it is poured out. But if the כהן went ahead and put it outside first and then inside, both kinds of blood reached their places, and the order does no harm.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Blood that is put inside the היכל
Blood that is put on the outer altar
The drain channel in the courtyard
Fit, valid

phrases.english: Mishnah:
Blood that is put inside
that got mixed with blood that is put outside
should be poured into the drain.
If he put it outside
and then put it inside, it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, after the earlier discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An inner/outer mixture is poured out at the start, but if it was put outside and then inside, it is fit.

steps.title: משנה: put inside first, then outside
steps.stepSummary: If the כהן put the mixture inside first and then outside, רבי עקיבא says it is פסול and the חכמים say it is fit. The argument is whether any blood that entered the היכל becomes פסול, or only a חטאת. רבי אליעזר adds the אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he put it inside and then outside, רבי עקיבא says it is פסול and the חכמים say it is fit. For רבי עקיבא says: all blood that entered to atone in the היכל is פסול. The חכמים say: only a חטאת. רבי אליעזר says: the אשם too, as it says, 'Like the חטאת, so the אשם.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the opposite order, inside first and then outside, and records an argument about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the mixture went into the היכל, the outer blood in it also entered the היכל. רבי עקיבא holds that this makes any such blood פסול, so putting it outside afterward does not help. The חכמים limit this rule to a חטאת, and רבי אליעזר widens it to an אשם based on a פסוק that compares the two.

keyTerms.meaning: Rules it disqualified
Rule it fit
To atone in the היכל
Sin offering
Guilt offering

steps.confusionAlert: The disqualifying problem here is the outer blood being brought into the היכל. Putting inner blood outside is not the issue in this argument.

phrases.english: If he put it inside and then put it outside,
Rabbi Akiva disqualifies it,
and the Sages declare it fit.
For Rabbi Akiva says:
All blood that entered
to atone in the Sanctuary is disqualified,
and the Sages say: only a sin offering.
Rabbi Eliezer says: the guilt offering too,
as it says: "Like the sin offering, so the guilt offering."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with the reverse order, inside first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא: any outer blood that entered the היכל is פסול. חכמים: only a חטאת. רבי אליעזר: an אשם too.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי אליעזר argue about the mixture too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אליעזר does not argue about the first case of the משנה (inner blood mixed with outer blood), just as he argues about the mixture of blood for above and below the red line.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Let רבי אליעזר argue about this case too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה with a challenge. It sets up the next move: explaining why רבי אליעזר stays silent here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier case of blood for above and below the red line, רבי אליעזר treated the wrongly placed blood as if it were water and allowed it to be used. If so, the same reasoning should apply to inner and outer blood, so why does the משנה record no argument from him?

keyTerms.meaning: And let him argue
In this case

phrases.english: Gemara:
And let Rabbi Eliezer argue about this case too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the first ruling of the new משנה (step 19).
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's unopposed ruling that an inner/outer mixture is poured out
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר's view on the above/below mixture (misplaced blood counts like water) should lead him to argue here as well.

steps.title: There is no proper order for the כהן to follow, so רבי אליעזר stays silent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי אליעזר's approach cannot work for inner and outer blood. Putting the blood outside first and then inside would break the rule that inner blood comes before outer blood. That rule works just like the rule that upper blood comes before lower blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: How should the כהן do it? Should he put the blood outside first and then put it inside? That cannot be. Just as it is a מצוה to put the upper blood before the lower blood, so too it is a מצוה to put the inside blood before the outside blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 21's question. It shows that using רבי אליעזר's method here would force the כהן to do things in the wrong order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case of upper and lower blood, רבי אליעזר lets the כהן treat the other blood as if it were water and put the blood on both places. Here, the גמרא pictures doing the same thing by putting the blood on the outer מזבח and then inside. That order is not allowed, because there is a מצוה to put the inner blood first, just as upper blood comes first. Since no proper order works, רבי אליעזר has nothing to argue about in this case.

keyTerms.meaning: How should he act? A question asking what practical steps could be taken
To put first, to give something an earlier turn
The upper ones: blood placed above the red line
The lower ones: blood placed below the red line
Inside: blood placed inside the היכל
Outside: blood placed on the outer מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר's approach only works when there is a proper order to follow. Inner blood must come before outer blood, just as upper blood comes before lower blood. Putting the outer blood first breaks that order, so his approach has no place in this case.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the rules about the order of placing blood can limit how far a lenient approach like רבי אליעזר's can go.

phrases.english: How should he act?
Should he place [it] outside
and then place [it] inside?
Just as it is a מצוה to put first
the upper [blood] before the lower,
so too it is a מצוה to put the inside [blood] before the outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי לֶיעְבֵּיד? נִיתֵּיב בַּחוּץ וַהֲדַר נִיתֵּיב לִפְנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21 about why רבי אליעזר does not argue about inner blood mixed with outer blood.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the case is different: a rule about the order of placing blood blocks רבי אליעזר's method here.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי אליעזר should argue here too, just as he argues about upper and lower blood.
steps.terutzMaskana: His method would mean putting the outside blood first, which breaks the rule that inside comes before outside, so he does not argue.
